Prayasvin Patel: 
Thank you, Harshit. Good evening, everyone, and welcome to Elecon Engineering's Q2 and H1 
FY '27 Earnings Conference Call. The earnings press release and investor presentation have 
been filed with the stock exchanges and are also available on our website. I will begin with the 
industry context, the operating environment and our performance during the quarter.  
 
Chintan will then discuss our financial results in great detail, after which we will take you 
through your questions.  
India's industrial outlook remains constructive, supported by public capital expenditure, 
infrastructure development and domestic manufacturing. Demand from cement and power, 
together with the anticipated threefold expansion in the steel production capacity, presents a 
substantial opportunity for the capital goods sector. 
 
Considering the industry research estimates, the Indian heavy-duty industrial gearbox market 
will grow at approximately 8% CAGR through FY '30. Key drivers include capacity creation, 
brownfield modernization and the need for efficient, reliable solutions. While global 
uncertainty, geopolitical developments and raw material volatility warrant continued vigilance, 
India's industrialization plans provide a strong and a durable foundation for long-term growth.  
 
At Elecon, our Gear and Material Handling Equipment divisions are distinct but complementary 
growth engines. Both serve critical industrial applications, and together, they give us the scale, 
technical breadth and market access to convert structural demand into sustained business 
growth. Over more than 7 decades, we have built a strong position in industrial gear solutions 
and material handling equipment. Our focus is clear; expand in overseas market, deepen our 
domestic footprint and execute with discipline and convert opportunities into profitable 
revenue growth. 

 
 
Elecon Engineering Company Limited

We will continue to protect margins, strengthen earnings quality and allocate resources to 
areas where Elecon has a durable competitive advantage. Our MHE division is now establishing 
a meaningful international presence, securing orders worth approximately USD9 million during 
the first half. This outcome validates the strategic decisions and capability building initiatives 
undertaken in recent years. 
 
It also demonstrates that our engineering expertise is competitive in global markets and gives 
us confidence in the division's international growth road map.  
In the Gear division, Elecon continues to strengthen its leadership in India's organized industrial 
gear market. Our comprehensive product portfolio, deep application expertise and ability to 
manufacture customized high-precision solutions meeting DIN Class 2 standards for critical 
applications have enabled us to build enduring relationships across key industry sectors. 
 
Turning to the MHE division, we see an increasingly important growth engine supported by 
established engineering capabilities and leadership in bulk material handling. Our record in 
complex applications and demanding project environments is difficult to replicate. We intend 
to build on this position by expanding in core industrial sectors and improving execution.  
 
Moving to segment-wise performance, the Gear division, which contributed approximately 
76% consolidated revenue in Q2 FY '27, reported revenue of INR488 crores, representing year-
on-year growth of 10.6%. This performance was led by 30.3% year-on-year growth in overseas 
markets, supported by stronger execution across international operations and sustained 
demand from overseas customers. Domestic demand remained stable. The result reinforces 
the value of our international strategy and the strength of our execution capabilities. 
 
The MHE division regained momentum in Q2 FY '27, reporting revenue of INR151 crores with 
year-on-year growth of 10.4%. Execution improved progressively compared with Q1, while 
demand from steel, power, cement, fertilizers and ports remains supportive. The division 
enters the second half with a clear execution agenda. 
 
Despite an uneven macroeconomic environment and delays in project execution clearances, 
our Q2 and H1 performance remained in line with expectations with consolidated revenue 
growing by 11% in H1. This outcome reflects the resilience of our diversified portfolio across 
Gear and MHE as well as growing contribution of international markets, which helped offset 
near-term softness in domestic activity. 
 
Our priorities for the second half are equally clear. We continue to build order pipeline and 
broaden our market footprint, maintain execution discipline and sustain profitable growth to 
navigate through volatile market environment. Elecon's strategy for the long term is anchored 
in 3 priorities: extend our reach across markets and applications, expand our engineering 
capabilities and execute consistently.

Our investments in R&D, technology and production development are directed towards 
practical customer outcomes, higher efficiency, reliability and life cycle value. This disciplined 
approach will broaden our addressable market, strengthen our competitive position and create 
a scalable platform for sustained growth. With that, I will hand over to our CFO, Mr. Chintan 
Shah, who will take you through the Q2 and H1 FY '27 financial performance in greater detail. 
Over to you, Chintan. 
Chintan Shah: 
Thank you, sir. I will take you through Elecon's financial performance for Q2 FY '27 and the first 
half, along with the key operating drivers. The results reflect disciplined execution and the 
resilience of our business model. Before discussing our financial performance, I am pleased to 
share 2 important developments. 
 
The outlook of the company's long-term credit rating has been upgraded from AA Stable to AA 
Positive, while its short-term rating has been reaffirmed at A1+. In addition, our lead banker 
has released the collateral security for both fund-based and non-fund-based working capital 
limits, thereby removing the hypothecation of movable and immovable properties, including 
plant and machinery. Both the above developments reflect the continued strengthening of our 
balance sheet and our growth outlook. 
 
Coming back to financial performance for Q2 FY '27: Revenue from operations increased 10.5% 
year-on-year to INR639 crores compared with INR578 crores in Q2 FY '26. When compared 
with revenue of INR521 crores in Q1 FY '27, your company has registered a growth of 22.7%. 
This reflects a clear acceleration in execution and improved conversion across our businesses. 
Profitability strengthened faster than revenue. EBITDA increased 17.7% to INR148 crores, while 
EBITDA margin expanded by 140 basis points to 23.1%. Profit after tax grew 9.8% to INR96 
crores with PAT margin at 15.1%. 
 
Financial performance for H1 FY '27: For like-to-like assessment, H1 FY '26 revenue and EBITDA 
are adjusted for INR25 crores of onetime arbitration settlement and income recorded in MHE. 
On this basis, H1 FY '27 revenue grew 11.1% year-on-year, demonstrating the underlying 
strength of our businesses. 
 
H1 EBITDA reached INR257 crores, up 11.4% over adjusted H1 FY '26 EBITDA. EBITDA margin 
was sustained at 22.2% compared with 22.1% in the corresponding adjusted period. This 
consistency demonstrates our ability to protect profitability while supporting the growth. Profit 
after tax was INR167 crores. Adjusted PAT increased 6.5%, excluding the after-tax impact of 
arbitration income and INR80 crores net of tax unrealized mark-to-market gain from 
reclassification of investments in the prior period. 
 
Now let me take you all through our segment-wise performance. Beginning with Gear division: 
The Gear division delivered a strong Q2 with revenue increasing 10.6% year-on-year to INR488 
crores. H1 revenue reached INR903 crores, representing growth of 13.1% with power 
remaining our high contributing industry. Profitability improved decisively. Q2 EBIT rose to 
27.2% to INR108 crores and EBIT margin expanded by 290 basis points to 22.1%.

H1 EBIT increased 21.8% to INR182 crores with margin at 20.2%. This demonstrates the earning

INR1,056 crores as of September 30, 2026. This is up by 37% year-on-year, providing strong H2 
visibility. 
 
Power, steel and cement, our 3 largest contributing industries, remain supported by India's 
midterm and long-term development priorities. With established technology, manufacturing 
depth and customer relationship, the Gear division is well equipped to translate demand into 
sustained earnings growth. 
 
Coming to Material Handling Equipment division: The MHE division delivered improved 
execution in Q2. Revenue increased 10.4% year-on-year to INR151 crores from INR137 crores. 
H1 revenue stood at INR256 crores, up 4.5% over adjusted H1 FY '26. With improved clearances 
on the projects, MHE has started scaling up the operations. We made tangible progress in Q2 
and are positioned to accelerate through the remainder of H2 FY '27. 
 
Demand indicators are encouraging. Q2 order intake increased 32.5% to INR253 crores. This 
includes overseas orders of INR68 crores. H1 order intake rose 34.8% to INR438 crores. The 
open order book reached to INR579 crores as of September 30, up 27.3% year-on-year. This 
provides sound execution visibility. 
 
Now coming back to geographical mix: Our overseas business continued to build momentum. 
Q2 overseas revenue increased 30.6% year-on-year to INR159 crores. H1 overseas revenue 
reached INR309 crores, with a growth of 26.2% year-on-year. Now overseas business 
contributes 27% of consolidated revenue compared with INR245 crores in H1 FY '26.  
Balance sheet and capital allocation: Elecon's financial position remains a strategic strength. As 
of September 30, 2026, shareholders' funds stood at INR2,509 crores. The balance sheet 
carried no conventional borrowings. 
 
The debt in our balance sheet primarily represents lease liabilities. This gives us resilience and 
capacity to invest. Working capital performance improved during H1 with the cycle towards 
normalizing to 89 days from 98 days in FY '26. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet 
with a net cash position of approximately INR700 crores. We also remain committed to our 
capital expenditure program for 3 years, which remains on track. 
 
Furthermore, we are pleased that the Board has declared an interim dividend of INR0.50 per 
equity share of face value of INR1 each, reaffirming our commitment to delivering value to our 
shareholders. As an outlook, as we enter the second half, our priorities are clear. 
 
We wish to accelerate MHE execution, convert the order pipeline with discipline, sustain 
margins and advance our international strategy. Given continued macroeconomic uncertainty 
and inflationary environment, but improved execution cycle, we are expecting a medium

welcome all your questions. Thank you.
